identification.title: I Surrender
identification.notes: Written by Matt Crocker, copyright 2011 Hillsong Music Publishing. CCLI 6177317. Recorded live October 2011 and released on Cornerstone in July 2012.

claims.structuralNotes: Verses and a repeated chorus, followed by two bridges that build and repeat at length. The final bridge is the song's emotional centre and carries most of its running time.

claims.claim: The singer hungers and thirsts for God's presence.
claims.subject: Desire for God

claims.claim: The singer gives everything over to God's will.
claims.subject: Surrender

claims.claim: The singer asks to know God relationally rather than merely about him.
claims.subject: The knowledge of God

claims.claim: The singer asks Jesus to breathe within them, as the Spirit indwelling.
claims.subject: The Holy Spirit

claims.claim: The singer asks to be consumed and remade by God's presence.
claims.subject: Sanctification

strengths.title: Surrender as the whole of the response
strengths.explanation: The song asks for nothing except that the singer be given over. In a genre that often asks God for outcomes, a song whose only request is to be handed over is doing something right.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Present your bodies as a living sacrifice — the offering the chorus makes.

strengths.title: Wants God rather than God's gifts
strengths.explanation: The object throughout is God himself, not relief or blessing. The hunger language is drawn straight from the psalms and keeps the song from becoming a request for circumstances to improve.
strengths.scriptureRationale: My soul thirsts for you, my flesh faints for you — the same appetite, and the same object.

strengths.title: Names Jesus and asks for the Spirit
strengths.explanation: The bridge is a request for the indwelling Spirit rather than for a feeling. It is the one place the song names Christ, and it echoes the moment Christ breathed on the disciples.
strengths.scriptureRationale: He breathed on them and said, Receive the Holy Spirit.

theological.assessment: Wants the right thing. The song's only request is that the singer be given over to God, and its object is God himself rather than his gifts — both rarer than they should be. What it never supplies is why. The cross is absent, and surrender is urged on the strength of the singer's hunger where Paul urges it on the mercies of God. Sound in its aim, resting on feeling for its motive.

strengths.title: Simple line, easily carried
strengths.explanation: The chorus is short and repeats a single phrase, so a congregation is not learning words while trying to mean them.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Commonly published in B flat and C. The verses sit comfortably; the repeated bridge is where an ordinary room stops singing.

range.key: Commonly published in B flat and C
range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: Extensive, and tied to a rising arrangement rather than to accumulating content. The repetition is doing the work the words are not.
communal.assessment: The words are easy enough to sing, but the song is shaped around a long build that a congregation cannot sustain and a platform can. Used as written it produces a room that listens through the section the song cares most about.

strengths.title: One idea, plainly said
strengths.explanation: The title is the message and the song does not wander from it. Nobody finishes unsure what was being offered.

clarity.assessment: Clear in what it says. The single idea is unmistakable, and the song leaves what surrender consists of to the teaching around it rather than spelling it out.

synthesis.summary: Its only request is that the singer be given over, and its object is God rather than his gifts — both rarer than they should be. But the cross is absent, and surrender rests on the singer's hunger where Paul rests it on God's mercies. Musically it is built around a long bridge most congregations hand back to the platform.

scriptureReferences.relevance: The offering the song makes, and the ground — God's mercies — it leaves out.
Thirst for God himself, which the verses draw on directly.
Christ breathing the Spirit on the disciples, echoed in the bridge.
Walking by faith rather than sight — the check the song does not provide.
